title: Squeezing the invisible
question: What happens to a trapped gas when you push on it?
hook: A gas fills whatever holds it, yet it can still be squeezed into less room.
idea: Gas particles are widely separated, so a gas spreads through its container and shrinks when pressure rises.

beats.prompt: You release gas at one end of an empty closed box. Where do its particles end up?

choices.label: Clustered near where they were released
choices.feedback: Gas particles spread apart rather than staying bunched up.

choices.label: Packed along the bottom
choices.feedback: That is how a liquid or solid might sit; gas particles distribute themselves throughout the container.

beats.explain: Gas particles spread apart to distribute themselves evenly throughout any container.

beats.prompt: When measuring a gas, sort each quantity by what it describes.
beats.explain: Measured characteristics are either in terms of the particles (velocity, pressure, temperature) or their surroundings (volume).

beats.prompt: One step in this account of Boyle's experiment is wrong. Which?
steps: Boyle trapped a gas in the closed end of a J-shaped tube.
The number of particles and the temperature stayed constant.
He added mercury, and the pressure on the gas rose, so its volume grew.
The pressure and volume of a gas therefore have an inverse relationship.
beats.explain: When the pressure was increased, the trapped gas's volume decreased, which is what makes the relationship inverse.

beats.prompt: You compare a 1-liter container of gas with a 1-liter container of liquid. Which holds fewer particles?

choices.label: The liquid, since its particles are far apart
choices.feedback: It is the gas whose particles are vastly separated.

choices.label: The gas, since its particles are far apart
Both hold exactly the same number
choices.feedback: Gases have low density compared with other states, so equal volumes do not hold equal numbers.

beats.explain: Gas particles are vastly separated and gases have low density compared with other states of matter.
